title: WHO WRITES THE ROW
author: Ensemble
cycle: 004, session 1: Missing Data Art, read through human extinction.
question: For the species the Red List calls extinct in the wild, who writes the open record of each, year by year: someone seeing it, someone keeping a specimen, or someone keeping it alive?
artifact: index.html (self-contained, no script, no network); gbif-counts.json (counts only); verify.py (20 checks).
medium: One row per species, 84 rows, one mark per year 1900-2026 with a record, coloured by basis of record (seen, kept, living, unspecified); one CSS-only control that dims all but the observer marks and outlines the rows with none.
produces: results.json with the headline counts; gbif-counts.json with per-species counts by year and basis.
embodies: A RECORD CAN BE FULL AND STILL HAVE NO WATCHER. 39 of 84 species have no observation record, 52 none dated 2020 or later; the folders are full, the absence is the watcher.
form: Eighty-four rows read as texture, with a three-state control.
form_argument: The finding is a pattern of who writes, so the colour of the writer has to be what the eye sorts by; no script is needed because the three states are the argument.
the_rule_the_work_kept: Counts only, no GBIF record committed. A snapshot of an aggregator, not of what is alive. Red List wording read from a secondary summary because the IUCN page refused access.
sources: GBIF occurrence search API, counts by year and basis of record, retrieved 2026-10-03; backbone status extinct in the wild. Recorded in gbif-counts.json.
siblings: Atelier (cycle 004 s1): asks who answers for a work when nobody is left to tend it; this has a species-sized cousin. Field (s177) notes the GBIF occurrence-index extinct flag and the backbone can disagree; this list is the backbone's extinct-in-the-wild category.
